title: Colorado Households by AMI
text:
The Colorado State Demography Office is assembling a reproducible workflow to estimate historic households by Area Median Income (AMI) and tenure, then forecast future demand informed by SDO household projections. These reports are organized as a Quarto website so the analyses share consistent formatting, navigation, and metadata.

Colorado Historical — constructs the ACS PUMS microdata pipeline, calculates AMI groupings, and loads results to the econ.cost_burden_by_ami table.
Forecast — allocates SDO household projections into AMI-by-tenure groups using the recent three-year average distribution.
United States — reproduces the historical pipeline for the U.S. to provide a national reference point.

title: Colorado Households by AMI
text:
Data requirements
Rendering the full site requires network access and credentials for:

SDO Postgres (read/write to econ and estimates schemas)
Google Drive project folder households_by_ami
IPUMS extracts usa_00104 and usa_00107
HUD API key available as HUD_API_KEY

Local disk storage under data/ stores cached extracts, parquet outputs, and CSV exports. Large intermediate objects can exhaust memory; the flexiblas configuration in the shared setup file constrains thread usage.

title: Colorado Households by AMI
text:
Rendering the site

Install Quarto 1.4 or later and required R packages (see README).
Place secrets in .Renviron (database URL, HUD key, Google tokens).
Run quarto render from the project root to build all pages.
Use quarto preview for iterative development with live reload.

If data access is unavailable, individual pages can be rendered with quarto render households_by_ami.qmd --execute-dir . to reuse existing cached outputs.

This script is used to pull the number of households by AMI in the United States using PUMS data via IPUMS using the ipumsr package.

source("_common.R")

title: Households by AMI US
text:
Household Data (IPUMS)
PUMS data is extracted using IPUMS USA data collection (Ruggles et al. 2024). The dataset and accompanying application have been created as a way of extracting and standardizing PUMS data for analysis. Data is extracted using the ipumsr package (Greg Freedman Ellis, Derek Burk, and Finn Roberts 2024).
First we get a list of all ACS samples, and filter to those with the pattern us20\d{2}a. This pattern matches all ACS 1 year samples available from 2000 onward, and are used to feed the query from IPUMS. Only samples beginning in 2005 will be used, however, as PUMA data is not available for Colorado prior to that year, and additionally during the period of 2000 to 2004 the ACS was more limited in scope and sample, only surveying 0.4% of the population, as opposed to 1% in years beginning in 2005.


Show code
acs_samples <- get_sample_info("usa") |>
  filter(str_detect(name, pattern = "us20\\d{2}a")) |>
  pull(name)


Next an extract is created and processed. The following table includes relevant variables and their definitions:

IPUMS Variables


Variable
Description




YEAR
Census year


SAMPLE
IPUMS sample identifier


SERIAL
Household serial number


CBSERIAL
Original Census Bureau household serial number


NUMPREC
Number of person records following


HHWT
Household weight


HHTYPE
Household Type


CLUSTER
Household cluster for variance estimation


CPI99
CPI-U adjustment factor to 1999 dollars


STATEFIP
State (FIPS code)


COUNTYFIP
County (FIPS code, identifiable counties only)


PUMA
Public Use Microdata Area


STRATA
Household strata for variance estimation


GQ
Group quarters status


OWNERSHP
Ownership of dwelling (tenure) [general version]


OWNERSHPD
Ownership of dwelling (tenure) [detailed version]


OWNCOST
Selected monthly owner costs


RENT
Monthly contract rent


RENTGRS
Monthly gross rent


HHINCOME
Total household income


BEDROOMS
Number of bedrooms


PERNUM
Person number in sample unit


PERWT
Person weight


FAMUNIT
Family unit membership


FAMSIZE
Number of own family members in household


NCHILD
Number of own children in the household


NCHLT5
Number of own children under age 5 in household


RELATE
Relationship to household head [general version]


RELATED
Relationship to household head [detailed version]


SEX
Sex


AGE
Age


RACE
Race [general version]


RACED
Race [detailed version]


HISPAN
Hispanic origin [general version]


HISPAND
Hispanic origin [detailed version]


BPL
Birthplace [general version]


BPLD
Birthplace [detailed version]


CITIZEN
Citizenship status


INCTOT
Total personal income


FTOTINC
Total family income


INCWAGE
Wage and salary income


INCBUS00
Business and farm income, 2000


INCSS
Social Security income


INCWELFR
Welfare (public assistance) income


INCINVST
Interest, dividend, and rental income


INCSUPP
Supplementary Security Income


INCOTHER
Other income


INCEARN
Total personal earned income


POVERTY
Poverty status


CBPOVERTY
Poverty status (original Census Bureau calculation)


MOVEDIN
When occupant moved into residence



The output of the IPUMS query is a data frame that includes a record for each household in Colorado from the ACS 1-year samples since 2000. Each record represents a person, with the head of household identified as person 1, and all other persons in the household following. This is based on the rectangular record format from IPUMS, rather than hierachal, as the household records lack necessary data for the analysis, such as person ages, or number of children in the household.


Show code
ipums_query <- "00107"
ipums_dir <- paste0(data_dir, "/ipums_raw")
# check if ipums files are in the data folder
ipums_files <- paste0("usa_", ipums_query, c(".csv.gz", ".xml"))
ipums_ddi <- file.path(ipums_dir, ipums_files[2])

# Load the IPUMS data from RDS file if it exists
if (sdo_drive_check_local(ipums_files, ipums_dir)) {
  acs_us_ddi <- read_ipums_ddi(ipums_ddi)

  ipums_us_duckplyr <- read_parquet_duckdb(
    "data/ipums_parquet/",
    prudence = "lavish"
  )
} else {
  sdo_drive_download(
    ipums_files,
    ipums_dir,
    project_folder = "households_by_ami"
  )
  if (sdo_drive_check_local(ipums_files, ipums_dir)) {
    acs_data_us <- read_ipums_ddi(ipums_ddi) |>
      read_ipums_micro()
  } else {
    acs_extract_us <- define_extract_micro(
      collection = "usa",
      description = "ACS 1 year samples in US of income variables, all samples since 2000",
      samples = acs_samples,
      variables = list(
        "STATEFIP",
        "NUMPREC",
        "CPI99",
        "OWNERSHP",
        "OWNCOST",
        "RENT",
        "RENTGRS",
        "RELATE",
        "HHTYPE",
        "HHINCOME",
        "INCTOT",
        "INCWAGE",
        "INCBUS00",
        "INCSS",
        "INCWELFR",
        "INCINVST",
        "INCSUPP",
        "INCOTHER",
        "INCEARN",
        "POVERTY",
        "CBPOVERTY",
        "AGE",
        "FAMUNIT",
        "FAMSIZE",
        "NCHILD",
        "NCHLT5",
        "FTOTINC",
        "BEDROOMS",
        "MOVEDIN"
      ),
      data_format = "csv"
    ) |>
      submit_extract() |>
      wait_for_extract() |>
      download_extract()

    # convert to parquet files by year
    ipums_us_duckplyr_csv <- read_csv_duckdb(
      "data/ipums_raw/usa_00107.csv.gz",
      prudence = "stingy"
    )
    map(c(2000:2024), \(x) {
      ipums_us_duckplyr_csv |>
        filter(YEAR == x) |>
        compute_parquet(paste0("data/ipums_parquet/ipums_", x, ".parquet"))
    })

    sdo_drive_upload(
      ipums_files,
      ipums_dir,
      project_folder = "households_by_ami"
    )
  }
}



Median Family Income
Median family income must be included in order to assign households into an Area Median Income (“AMI”) grouping based on Household Income. There are two potential sources of Median Family Income data - the published AMI published annually by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”), or the American Community Survey (“ACS”), created annually by the United States Census Bureau (“CB”).
While both HUD and ACS data were obtained and processed, only the ACS data was ultimately used, primarily for comparability to the state and region calculations. HUD data is only available at the state and county levels, and not nationally.
There are benefits and drawbacks to each approach though primarily this is done to align with the rest of the analysis, and because a national MFI does not existed (it could be approximated using weighted averages of state level HUD data, but this would be less accurate). In particular, HUD data is specifically designed for use in housing policy and programs, while ACS median family income is a more general measure of income.
The primary reason for using ACS median family income (in addition to the regional availability) is that it most accurately describes the actual income distribution in a given year, as it is based on that specific sample, while the HUD data is estimated annually using the most recently available ACS data and inflation adjusting it forward. Because of this, these amounts won’t be the same, and the HUD MFI’s will tend to be biased downward in years where incomes are rising faster than inflation, and biased upward in years where incomes are rising slower than inflation or declining. When real incomes are falling (i.e., inflation is rising faster than nominal income), the HUD MFI’s will be biased upward relative to actual incomes. We see this arrising in the data.
Ultimately the decision to use ACS MFI’s was made based on the desire to have the most accurate representation of income distributions in the United States, and to align with the rest of this analysis. Additionally, a similar method is used in the HUD Consolidated Planning/CHAS dataset, which is commonly used for housing needs assessments, and so this approach more closely aligns with this methodology (Joice 2014).

ACS PUMS
This data needed to be created by calculating the median family income from the ACS PUMS data itself. This is handled by creating a generic function based on design object using the srvyr package, and then calculating the median family income by year for each region1.


Show code
# create function for calculating mfi by year
get_mfi_us <- function(YEAR) {
  parquet_file <- paste0("data/ipums_parquet/ipums_", YEAR, ".parquet")

  mfi_df <- read_parquet_duckdb(parquet_file) |>
    filter(
      # YEAR == 2000,
      PERNUM == 1, # One record per household
      GQ %in% c(1, 2) # Households and group quarters
    ) |>
    as_survey_design(
      weight = HHWT,
      # repweights = matches("REPWT[0-9]+"),
      type = "ACS",
      mse = TRUE
    ) |>
    filter(
      # PERNUM == 1, # One record per household
      # GQ %in% c(1, 2), # Households and group quarters
      FTOTINC != 9999999, # Exclude missing values
      FTOTINC > 0, # Positive income only
      FAMSIZE >= 2 # Families have 2+ members
    ) |>
    group_by(YEAR) |>
    summarize(
      mfi = survey_median(as.numeric(FTOTINC))
    )

  return(mfi_df)
}

# load data if saved otherwise calculate for all years
if (!file.exists("data/us_mfi_from_pums_us.parquet")) {
  # First create MFI's by PUMA
  mfi_from_pums_us <- map(2000:2024, get_mfi_us, .progress = TRUE)

  compute_parquet(
    bind_rows(mfi_from_pums_us),
    "data/us_mfi_from_pums_us.parquet"
  )
} else {
  mfi_from_pums_us <- read_parquet_duckdb("data/us_mfi_from_pums_us.parquet") |>
    collect()
}





Modify IPUMS Data
Next a series of calculations are performed to modify the IPUMS data to be more useful for analysis. The following table includes the variables generated and their descriptions.







Variable Name
Description




hhsize
Household size - equal, to the total number of person records, NUMREC)


nadults
Number of adults in the household - total number of persons records - number of children (NUMREC - NCHILD)


household_type_id
Household type - a factor variable with four levels: “One adult with no children”, “One adult with children”, “More than one adult with no children”, “More than one adult with children” - based on characteristics of the household


age_group
Age group - a factor variable with five levels: “Under 18”, “18-24”, “25-44”, “45-64”, “65 and over” - based on the age of the person


hhadj
An adjustment factor to apply to household income based on the size of the household


mfi_hh
Household median family income - household income adjusted for household size


pct_mfi
Percent of median family income - household income divided by the median family income


ami_group
Grouping of households by Median Family Income


ami_percentile
Percent of median family income based on 10 percentile groups


housing_cost_pct
Housing cost as a percentage of income



Of particular importance is the method for calculating percentage of median family income, which is based on the adjusted median family income as determined by household size. This is done by first applying an adjustment factor based on Median Family Income (based on HUD calculations), and then applying this adjustment factor to actual Median Family Income, to get a size adjusted MFI that household income can be compared to. Household income is then divided by this adjusted MFI to get the percentage of median family income, used for binning and grouping.
Cost burdened status is taken by dividing housing costs by household income. Housing costs are based either on the RENT2 variable for renter households, or the OWNCOST variable for owner households, and are assigned based on tenure of the household. Housing costs are each reported on a monthly basis, and so must be annualized by multiplying by 12, prior to dividing by household income.
A generic function is created to perform these calculations, and then applied to both the state-level and region-level datasets.


Show code
# create function for calculating necessary variables and adding them to acs_amis_us
prep_amis <- function(mfi_year, mfi) {
  acs_amis_us <- ipums_us_duckplyr |>
    filter(YEAR == mfi_year) |>
    mutate(
      nadults = NUMPREC - NCHILD,
      hhsize = NUMPREC,
      household_type_id = (case_when(
        nadults == 1 & NCHILD == 0 ~ "One adult with no children    ",
        nadults == 1 & NCHILD > 0 ~ "One adult with children",
        nadults > 1 & NCHILD == 0 ~ "More than one adult with no children",
        nadults > 1 & NCHILD > 0 ~ "More than one adult with children"
      )),
      age_group = as.character(
        cut(
          AGE,
          breaks = c(
            0,
            18,
            25,
            45,
            65,
            Inf
          ),
          labels = c(
            "Under 18",
            "18-24",
            "25-44",
            "45-64",
            "65 and over"
          ),
          right = FALSE,
          ordered_result = FALSE
        )
      ),
      hhadj = case_when(
        hhsize < 4 ~ 1 - (4 - hhsize) * .1,
        hhsize >= 4 ~ 1 + (hhsize - 4) * .08,
        .default = 1
      ),
      mfi_hh = mfi * hhadj,
      pct_mfi = HHINCOME / mfi_hh,
      ami_group = as.character(
        cut(
          pct_mfi,
          breaks = c(
            0,
            .3,
            .5,
            .8,
            1,
            Inf
          ),
          labels = c(
            "Less than 30",
            "30 to 50",
            "50 to 80",
            "80 to 100",
            "Greater than 100"
          ),
          right = FALSE,
          ordered_result = FALSE
        )
      ),
      ami_percentile = ceiling(pct_mfi * 10) / 10,
      tenure = case_when(
        OWNERSHP == 1 ~ "Owner",
        OWNERSHP == 2 ~ "Renter",
        TRUE ~ "Other"
      ),
      # tenure_detail = (OWNERSHPD),
      housing_cost = case_when(
        OWNERSHP == 2 ~ RENT * 12,
        OWNERSHP == 1 ~ OWNCOST * 12,
        .default = NA_real_
      ),
      housing_cost_pct = housing_cost / HHINCOME,
      cost_burdened_30 = case_when(
        housing_cost_pct >= .3 ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      ),
      cost_burdened_50 = case_when(
        housing_cost_pct >= .5 ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      )
    )
}

if (!file.exists("data/ami_parquet/ami_2000mfi.parquet")) {
  acs_us <- map2(
    mfi_from_pums_us$YEAR,
    mfi_from_pums_us$mfi,
    ~ prep_amis(.x, .y) |>
      compute_parquet(paste0("data/ami_parquet/ami_", .x, "mfi.parquet")),
    .progress = TRUE
  )
}

rm(ipums_us_duckplyr)

title: Households by AMI
text:
Per C.R.S. 24-32-3702(1)(b),

(b) No later than November 30, 2027, and every six years thereafter, the director shall conduct a statewide housing needs assessment that analyzes existing and future statewide housing needs. The director shall publish a report based on the statewide housing needs assessment and regional and local housing needs assessments accepted by the department pursuant to section 24-32-3703 (3) or 24-32-3704 (3) that identifies current housing stock and estimates the number and type of dwelling units needed to accommodate future housing needs of the state based on population change projections. The report shall categorize statewide housing needs by household size; household type, including accessible, visitable, supportive, affordable for-sale, and affordable rental housing; and household income levels, including extremely low-, very low-, low-, moderate-, and middle-income households as designated by the United States department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”).

In pursuing these requirements, we will begin by establishing a historic time series of housing data, including the number of housing units by type and income level, utilizing data from the Census Bureau’s Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS), and then forecast future marginal demand based on our projections of total households by type.

title: Households by AMI
text:
Data Collection
This script is used to pull the number of households by AMI in Colorado using PUMS data via IPUMS using the ipumsr package. Median Family Incomes are collected separately as provided by HUD, using the tidycensus package.


Show code
source("_common.R")
library(ipumsr)
library(srvyr)
library(tidycensus)
library(duckplyr)
library(hudr)
library(googledrive)

hud_key <- Sys.getenv("HUD_API_KEY")
if (identical(hud_key, "")) {
  stop("HUD_API_KEY is not set in the environment.")
}

# load region crosswalk from sdo database
xwalk_puma_region <- pull_db_table("xwalk", "hna_puma_region")

data_dir <- "data"
ipums_query <- "00104"

    mutate(

        YEAR < 2012 ~ "PUMA00",
        YEAR < 2022 ~ "PUMA10",

    left_join(
      xwalk_puma_region |>
        # join region crosswalk to acs_data
        mutate(PUMA = as.integer(puma)) |>

      by = c("puma_year", "PUMA")

    # use lowercase variable names
    rename_with(tolower)

Median Family Income
Median family income must be included in order to assign households into an Area Median Income (“AMI”) grouping based on Household Income. There are two potential sources of Median Family Income data - the published AMI published annually by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”), or the American Community Survey (“ACS”), created annually by the United States Census Bureau (“CB”).
While both HUD and ACS data were obtained and processed, only the ACS data was ultimately used, as it provides more granular data at the PUMA level, which allows for regional analysis within Colorado. HUD data is only available at the state and county levels.
There are benefits and drawbacks to each approach at the state level as actual PUMA region data is only available using the ACS microdata (it could be approximated using weighted averages of county level HUD data, but this would be less accurate). In particular, HUD data is specifically designed for use in housing policy and programs, while ACS median family income is a more general measure of income.
The primary reason for using ACS median family income (in addition to the regional availability) is that it most accurately describes the actual income distribution in a given year, as it is based on that specific sample, while the HUD data is estimated annually using the most recently available ACS data and inflation adjusting it forward. Because of this, these amounts won’t be the same, and the HUD MFI’s will tend to be biased downward in years where incomes are rising faster than inflation, and biased upward in years where incomes are rising slower than inflation or declining. Additionally, HUD MFI’s use the United States Consumer Price Index (“CPI”) to adjust for inflation, which may additionally bias the results. When real incomes are falling (i.e., inflation is rising faster than nominal income) or US CPI is rising faster than local inflation, the HUD MFI’s will be biased upward relative to actual incomes. We see this arrising in the data, as during the 2010s (when both Colorado incomes and inflation were outpacing the US), the HUD MFI’s were lower than the ACS MFIs, while this trend reversed during the early 2020s, when inflation rose rapidly at the US level, and Colorado inflation somewhat lagged.
Ultimately the decision to use ACS MFI’s was made based on the desire to have the most accurate representation of income distributions in Colorado, particularly at the regional level, and to avoid potential biases introduced by inflation adjustments and national CPI data. Additionally, a similar method is used in the HUD Consolidated Planning/CHAS dataset, which is commonly used for housing needs assessments, and so this approach more closely aligns with this methodology (Joice 2014).
Finally, it was decided to use the PUMA level esimates and aggregate them to the state level, rather than to estimate the state level directly. This was done primarily to maintain consistency between the state and regional estimates (i.e., so the state would sum to the total of the regions), and because it allows for somewhat more detail by allowing for region level median family incomes to be applied against households, rather than using a single statewide MFI for all households.

HUD
Initially, Median Family Income files were downloaded from the HUD website and stored as acs_mfi using r_scripts/read_hud_amis.R. This data was not ultimately used, but is included here for reference.


ACS PUMS
This data needed to be created by calculating the median family income from the ACS PUMS data itself. This is handled by creating a generic function based on design object using the srvyr package, and then calculating the median family income by year for each region1.


Show code
# Create survey design object
acs_srvy <- acs_data |>
  filter(
    year >= 2005, # remove years without puma data, skip 2000
    pernum == 1, # one record per household
    gq %in% c(1, 2) # households and group quarters
  ) |>
  as_survey_design(
    weight = hhwt,
    repweights = matches("repwt[0-9]+"),
    type = "acs",
    mse = true
  )

# first create mfi's by region
mfi_region <- acs_srvy |>
  filter(
    pernum == 1, # one record per household
    gq %in% c(1, 2), # households and group quarters
    ftotinc != 9999999, # exclude missing values
    ftotinc > 0, # positive income only
    famsize >= 2 # families have 2+ members
  ) |>
  group_by(year, region) |>
  summarize(
    mfi = survey_median(as.numeric(ftotinc))
  )

# create median household income by region
mhi_region <- acs_srvy |>
  filter(
    pernum == 1, # one record per household
    gq %in% c(1, 2), # households and group quarters
    hhincome != 9999999, # exclude missing values
    hhincome > 0 # positive income only
  ) |>
  group_by(year, region) |>
  summarize(
    mhi = survey_median(as.numeric(hhincome))
  )

# mfi_state <- acs_srvy |>
#   filter(
#     pernum == 1, # one record per household
#     gq %in% c(1, 2), # households and group quarters
#     ftotinc != 9999999, # exclude missing values
#     ftotinc > 0, # positive income only

#   summarize(
#     region = "0",
#     mfi = survey_median(as.numeric(ftotinc))
#   )





Modify IPUMS Data
Next a series of calculations are performed to modify the IPUMS data to be more useful for analysis. The following table includes the variables generated and their descriptions.







Variable Name
Description




hhsize
Household size - equal, to the total number of person records, NUMREC)


nadults
Number of adults in the household - total number of persons records - number of children (NUMREC - NCHILD)


household_type_id
Household type - a factor variable with four levels: “One adult with no children”, “One adult with children”, “More than one adult with no children”, “More than one adult with children” - based on characteristics of the household


age_group
Age group - a factor variable with five levels: “Under 18”, “18-24”, “25-44”, “45-64”, “65 and over” - based on the age of the person


hhadj
An adjustment factor to apply to household income based on the size of the household


mfi_hh
Household median family income - household income adjusted for household size


pct_mfi
Percent of median family income - household income divided by the median family income


ami_group
Grouping of households by Median Family Income


ami_percentile
Percent of median family income based on 10 percentile groups


housing_cost_pct
Housing cost as a percentage of income



Of particular importance is the method for calculating percentage of median family income, which is based on the adjusted median family income as determined by household size. This is done by first applying an adjustment factor based on Median Family Income (based on HUD calculations), and then applying this adjustment factor to actual Median Family Income, to get a size adjusted MFI that household income can be compared to. Household income is then divided by this adjusted MFI to get the percentage of median family income, used for binning and grouping.
Cost burdened status is taken by dividing housing costs by household income. Housing costs are based either on the RENT2 variable for renter households, or the OWNCOST variable for owner households, and are assigned based on tenure of the household. Housing costs are each reported on a monthly basis, and so must be annualized by multiplying by 12, prior to dividing by household income.
A generic function is created to perform these calculations, and then applied to both the state-level and region-level datasets.


Show code
fn_calculate_pums <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      nadults = numprec - nchild,
      hhsize = numprec,
      household_type_id = str_to_title(case_when(
        nadults == 1 & nchild == 0 ~ "one adult with no children",
        nadults == 1 & nchild > 0 ~ "one adult with children",
        nadults > 1 & nchild == 0 ~ "more than one adult with no children",
        nadults > 1 & nchild > 0 ~ "more than one adult with children"
      )),
      age_group = cut(
        age,
        breaks = c(
          0,
          18,
          25,
          45,
          65,
          Inf
        ),
        labels = c(
          "Under 18",
          "18-24",
          "25-44",
          "45-64",
          "65 and Over"
        ),
        right = FALSE,
        ordered_result = TRUE
      ),
      hhadj = case_when(
        hhsize < 4 ~ 1 - (4 - hhsize) * .1,
        hhsize >= 4 ~ 1 + (hhsize - 4) * .08,
        .default = 1
      ),
      mfi_hh = mfi * hhadj,
      pct_mfi = hhincome / mfi_hh,
      ami_group = cut(
        pct_mfi,
        breaks = c(
          0,
          .3,
          .5,
          .8,
          1,
          1.2,
          Inf
        ),
        labels = c(
          "Less than 30",
          "30 to 50",
          "50 to 80",
          "80 to 100",
          "100 to 120",
          "Greater than 120"
        ),
        right = FALSE,
        ordered_result = TRUE
      ),
      ami_percentile = ceiling(pct_mfi * 10) / 10,
      tenure = as_factor(ownershp),
      tenure_detail = as_factor(ownershpd),
      housing_cost = case_when(
        ownershp == 2 ~ rentgrs * 12,
        ownershp == 1 ~ owncost * 12,
        .default = NA_real_
      ),
      housing_cost_pct = pmin((housing_cost / hhincome) * 100, 101),
      calc_housing_cost = case_when(
        ownershp == 2 & rentgrs > 0 & hhincome > 0 ~ TRUE,
        ownershp == 1 & hhincome > 0 ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      ),
      cost_burdened_30 = case_when(
        housing_cost_pct >= 30 & calc_housing_cost ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      ),
      cost_burdened_50 = case_when(
        housing_cost_pct >= 50 & calc_housing_cost ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      )
    ) |>
    zap_labels()
}

#   mutate(region = "0") |>
#   inner_join(
#     mfi_state,
#     by = c("year", "region")
#   ) |>

acs_amis_region <- acs_data |>
  inner_join(
    mfi_region,
    by = c("year", "region")
  ) |>
  fn_calculate_pums()

title: Households by AMI
text:
Per C.R.S. 24-32-3702(1)(b),

(b) No later than November 30, 2027, and every six years thereafter, the director shall conduct a statewide housing needs assessment that analyzes existing and future statewide housing needs. The director shall publish a report based on the statewide housing needs assessment and regional and local housing needs assessments accepted by the department pursuant to section 24-32-3703 (3) or 24-32-3704 (3) that identifies current housing stock and estimates the number and type of dwelling units needed to accommodate future housing needs of the state based on population change projections. The report shall categorize statewide housing needs by household size; household type, including accessible, visitable, supportive, affordable for-sale, and affordable rental housing; and household income levels, including extremely low-, very low-, low-, moderate-, and middle-income households as designated by the United States department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”).

In pursuing these requirements, we will begin by establishing a historic time series of housing data, including the number of housing units by type and income level, utilizing data from the Census Bureau’s Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS), and then forecast future marginal demand based on our projections of total households by type.

source("_common.R")

text:
Household Data (IPUMS)
PUMS data is extracted using IPUMS USA data collection (Ruggles et al. 2024). The dataset and accompanying application have been created as a way of extracting and standardizing PUMS data for analysis. Data is extracted using the ipumsr package (Greg Freedman Ellis, Derek Burk, and Finn Roberts 2024).
First we get a list of all ACS samples, and filter to those with the pattern us20\d{2}a. This pattern matches all ACS 1 year samples available from 2000 onward, and are used to feed the query from IPUMS. Only samples beginning in 2005 will be used, however, as PUMA data is not available for Colorado prior to that year, and additionally during the period of 2000 to 2004 the ACS was more limited in scope and sample, only surveying 0.4% of the population, as opposed to 1% in years beginning in 2005.


Show code
acs_samples <- get_sample_info("usa") |>
  filter(str_detect(name, pattern = "us2024")) |>
  pull(name)

Variable
Description

The output of the IPUMS query is a data frame that includes a record for each household in Colorado from the ACS 1-year samples since 2000. Each record represents a person, with the head of household identified as person 1, and all other persons in the household following. This is based on the rectangular record format from IPUMS, rather than hierachal, as the household records lack necessary data for the analysis, such as person ages, or number of children in the household. PUMA regions are assigned using a manually created crosswalk between PUMA codes and the HNA regions as defined by SDO.


Show code
data_dir <- "data"
ipums_query <- "00113"
ipums_dir <- paste0(data_dir, "/ipums_raw")

ipums_ddi <- file.path(ipums_dir, ipums_files[2])

  acs_data <- read_ipums_ddi(ipums_ddi) |>
    read_ipums_micro() |>
    mutate(
      puma_year = case_when(
        YEAR < 2012 ~ "PUMA00",
        YEAR < 2022 ~ "PUMA10",
        .default = "PUMA20"
      )
    ) |>
    left_join(
      xwalk_puma_region |>
        # join region crosswalk to acs_data
        mutate(PUMA = as.integer(puma)) |>
        select(-puma),
      by = c("puma_year", "PUMA")
    ) |>
    # use lowercase variable names
    rename_with(tolower)

Of particular importance is the method for calculating percentage of median family income, which is based on the adjusted median family income as determined by household size. This is done by first applying an adjustment factor based on Median Family Income (based on HUD calculations), and then applying this adjustment factor to actual Median Family Income, to get a size adjusted MFI that household income can be compared to. Household income is then divided by this adjusted MFI to get the percentage of median family income, used for binning and grouping.
Cost burdened status is taken by dividing housing costs by household income. Housing costs are based either on the RENT2 variable for renter households, or the OWNCOST variable for owner households, and are assigned based on tenure of the household. Housing costs are each reported on a monthly basis, and so must be annualized by multiplying by 12, prior to dividing by household income.
A generic function is created to perform these calculations, and then applied to both the state-level and region-level datasets.


Show code
fn_calculate_pums <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      nadults = numprec - nchild,
      hhsize = numprec,
      household_type_id = str_to_title(case_when(
        nadults == 1 & nchild == 0 ~ "one adult with no children",
        nadults == 1 & nchild > 0 ~ "one adult with children",
        nadults > 1 & nchild == 0 ~ "more than one adult with no children",
        nadults > 1 & nchild > 0 ~ "more than one adult with children"
      )),
      age_group = cut(
        age,
        breaks = c(
          0,
          18,
          25,
          45,
          65,
          Inf
        ),
        labels = c(
          "Under 18",
          "18-24",
          "25-44",
          "45-64",
          "65 and Over"
        ),
        right = FALSE,
        ordered_result = TRUE
      ),
      hhadj = case_when(
        hhsize < 4 ~ 1 - (4 - hhsize) * .1,
        hhsize >= 4 ~ 1 + (hhsize - 4) * .08,
        .default = 1
      ),
      mfi_hh = mfi * hhadj,
      pct_mfi = hhincome / mfi_hh,
      ami_group = cut(
        pct_mfi,
        breaks = c(
          0,
          .3,
          .5,
          .8,
          1,
          1.2,
          Inf
        ),
        labels = c(
          "Less than 30",
          "30 to 50",
          "50 to 80",
          "80 to 100",
          "100 to 120",
          "Greater than 120"
        ),
        right = FALSE,
        ordered_result = TRUE
      ),
      ami_percentile = ceiling(pct_mfi * 10) / 10,
      tenure = as_factor(ownershp),
      tenure_detail = as_factor(ownershpd),
      housing_cost = case_when(
        ownershp == 2 ~ rentgrs * 12,
        ownershp == 1 ~ owncost * 12,
        .default = NA_real_
      ),
      housing_cost_pct = pmin((housing_cost / hhincome) * 100, 101),
      calc_housing_cost = case_when(
        ownershp == 2 & rentgrs > 0 & hhincome > 0 ~ TRUE,
        ownershp == 1 & hhincome > 0 ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      ),
      cost_burdened_30 = case_when(
        housing_cost_pct >= 30 & calc_housing_cost ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      ),
      cost_burdened_50 = case_when(
        housing_cost_pct >= 50 & calc_housing_cost ~ TRUE,
        .default = FALSE
      ),
      full_time = as.numeric(wkswork1) >= 45 & empstat == 1 & as.numeric(uhrswork) >= 35
    ) |> 
      mutate(any_employed = empstat == 1, .by = c()) |>
}


acs_amis_state <- acs_data |>
  mutate(region = "0") |>
  inner_join(
    mfi_state,
    by = c("year")
  ) |>
  fn_calculate_pums()
